title: Atomic profile upload + sparse metadata encoding to speed model onboarding
author: Sofia Park
description: Context: onboarding new variants (sparse/quantized forks and multi-variant archives) has been bottlenecked by two problems: 1) upload/commit window races when multiple artifacts (weights, tokenizer, profile JSON) are pushed independently; 2) blow-up in registry metadata size because we persist dense per-model performance vectors even when many metrics are sparse or absent. This PR introduces two complementary changes: an "atomic profile upload" API and a compact sparse metadata encoding for performance profiles. Goals: reduce partial/onboarding failures due to interleaved publishes, speed up commit-hooks for large batches, and shrink profile storage/transfer by ~4x for models with sparse measurements. Summary of changes (single-string): - Add POST /models/:id/atomic-profile endpoint in the registry API to accept a single gzipped tarball containing: model.tar (weights), tokenizer.json, profile.json, provenance.json. The endpoint validates schema and performs a single transactional commit that publishes the model and all artifacts together. - Introduce a compact sparse-vec encoding for profile.json: instead of storing a dense vector for all bench metrics, we store an index-value list and a small schema that maps metric ids to names. The registry still materializes dense view on-demand for queries. - Update onboard CLI (cli/onboard) to detect multi-file uploads and use the atomic endpoint by default. Adds a --legacy flag to keep previous behavior for backcompat. - Server-side migration job that scans recent profiles and converts dense profiles smaller than 8KB verbatim and compresses others into the new sparse format. Migration runs as a low-priority background job. - Add unit + integration tests around transactional commit, partial-failure rollbacks, and profile roundtrips. - Docs: REST API spec, CLI quickstart, and migration notes in docs/registry/onboarding.md Motivation and scope: this is focused on inference onboarding and registry durability; it intentionally avoids changing signing/key provenance or the release note generator pipeline (a follow-on PR will add signed release bundles). Checklist: - [x] API contract defined and documented - [x] CLI wired to use atomic endpoint - [x] Server commit/rollback logic implemented and tested - [x] Sparse encoding spec documented - [x] Migration job implemented and throttled - [x] End-to-end test with a 4-artifact tarball - [ ] Performance dashboard alert for migration impact (follow-up)
commits_summary: 7 commits: initial sparse-encoding prototype; atomic endpoint scaffold; transactional commit/rollback; onboard-cli switch + tests; migration worker + throttling; docs and OpenAPI update; e2e test harness + flake fixes.
files_changed_list: api/registry/atomic_profile_handler.py, registry/storage/atomic_commit.py, registry/profiles/sparse_codec.py, cli/onboard/command.py, migrations/2024_11_sparse_profile_migration.py, tests/registry/test_atomic_commit.py, tests/cli/test_onboard_atomic.py, docs/registry/onboarding.md, openapi/registry.yaml, infra/helm/values.yaml (config knob for migration rate).
review_conversation: Amit: asked for clarity on rollback guarantees when background cleanup fails; requested explicit idempotency key handling. Sofia: addressed by adding a txn id persisted in registry model row and a background reconciler that replays or aborts incomplete commits. Leah: raised concern about schema churn for downstream consumers of profile.json; requested a compatibility layer. Sofia: added a materialize API that returns the dense view and a feature-flag to enable sparse storage per-organization. Marco: ran load test and reported a transient 12% increase in DB write latency during migration start; we added throttling and low-priority worker queue. Final approvals: Amit (approved), Leah (approved), Marco (approved).
ci_log_summary: CI run 1: lint + unit tests: passed. CI run 2: integration tests hit a flaky network test causing a rerun; rerun passed. E2E job: initially failed due to missing gzip dependency in container (fixed in Dockerfile). All checks passed on final push. Coverage change: +0.6% on registry service.
ci_details: Checks: lint (pass), unit-tests (pass), integration-tests (pass after 1 rerun), e2e (pass), openapi-validate (pass), security-scan (pass). Note: migration job gated behind feature flag to avoid early rollout.
migration_notes: Migration runs with a default batch size of 50 profiles per minute (configurable via helm). It skips profiles already flagged as 'sparse_v2' and writes a migration marker per-model to avoid duplicate work. Rollback plan: disable migration flag and run a reconciliation job to rehydrate any materialized dense views if needed.
performance_impact: Benchmarks: onboarding end-to-end time for a 4-artifact bundle reduced from median 2.2s -> 1.05s under normal load (approx 52% improvement). Storage: typical profile payload for sparse datasets reduced 3.6-4.3x. Observability: added metrics registry.atomic_uploads.total, registry.atomic_uploads.failures, registry.profile_sparse_conversion.count.
release_notes: Add atomic multi-artifact onboarding endpoint and compact sparse profile encoding. Improves onboarding latency and reduces profile storage for sparse measurements. Migration will run in background; controlled via feature flag. No breaking changes to API consumers (dense materialize API remains available).
merge_outcome: Merged via squash on 2024-11-09 after reviewers approved and CI green. Changelog entry added to releases/2024-11.md. Backcompat: onboard CLI supports --legacy to use previous multi-call behavior; feature flag 'registry.use_sparse_profiles' defaults to false for 1 week rollout.
notes_for_follow_up: Follow-up tasks: 1) signed release bundle integration (ENG-2016). 2) add migration alert and rollback playbook in runbooks/registry-migration.md. 3) add telemetry for materialize API cost and cache hit rate. 4) Run a longer-duration migration in staging with 10x profile volume.
security_considerations: Tarball unpacking is sandboxed with a strict whitelist; content is validated against JSON schemas and size limits. CI includes a quick fuzzer run on uploader. Migration marks are integrity-checked to avoid replay attacks. KMS signing of provenance is out-of-scope for this PR and will be addressed separately.
human_readable_summary: This PR reduces model onboarding failures and speeds up large-bundle uploads by adding an atomic upload endpoint and compressing sparse performance profiles. Includes server-side migration and CLI changes, merged to main after tests and reviews.
